body:
Found while writing user-facing copy telling people to sync after a repair. The
copy could not be justified, and the reason it could not is the finding.

## What the repair actually does

`cps/tasks/kepub_package_repair.py:332` marks the book:

    helper.mark_book_modified(candidate, set_dirty=False, unsync=False)

`cps/helper.py:75` stamps `book.last_modified` and, ONLY when `unsync=True`,
calls `kobo_sync_status.remove_synced_book(book.id, all=True)` — which its own
docstring describes as the step that makes "every device re-pull". The repair
task passes `unsync=False`, so that step never runs.

## What the device receives

OBSERVED, `cps/kobo.py:1053` `create_book_entitlement`:

    "CrossRevisionId": book_uuid,
    "Id":              book_uuid,
    "RevisionId":      book_uuid,
    "Created":         book.timestamp,
    "LastModified":    book.last_modified,     <- the only field the repair changes

The repair rewrites bytes on disk. It does not change the book's UUID or its
`timestamp`. So the entitlement the device gets carries **the same revision
identity it already holds**, with a newer LastModified.

OBSERVED, `cps/kobo.py:655-660` + `get_kobo_created_ts` (`kobo.py:140`): the
NewEntitlement/ChangedEntitlement choice is `ts_created > sync_token.books_last_created`,
where `ts_created` comes from `Books.timestamp` / `date_added` — never from
`KoboSyncedBooks`. Once a device has synced a book, its cursor is past that
book's creation timestamp forever, so a repaired book emits **ChangedEntitlement
on every subsequent sync, unconditionally**.

## The part that is documented wrong, twice

Two places state that clearing `KoboSyncedBooks` is what produces a
NewEntitlement:

- `cps/admin.py:1445` — "Clears the (user_id, book_id) row from
  kobo_synced_books so the sync emits NewEntitlement"
- `tests/unit/test_kobo_admin_resend_book.py:81` — "without the deletion the
  next sync emits ChangedEntitlement rather than re-delivering the file"

The second is a SOURCE-PINNED test, so it asserts the string is present in
`do_kobo_resend` and never executes the claim. Per `get_kobo_created_ts`,
deleting that row cannot change the entitlement type — the type is decided
entirely by timestamps. Whatever makes `do_kobo_resend` work, the stated
mechanism is not it.

That matters beyond tidiness: this belief is what anyone would rely on to decide
whether the repair reaches devices, and it is load-bearing in exactly the place
nothing verifies it.

## What is genuinely unknown

UNOBSERVED: whether a Kobo re-downloads a book's file when it receives a
ChangedEntitlement whose RevisionId it already has. Nobody has measured it. The
repository's own comments assert it does not, but on a mechanism that does not
exist, so those comments are not evidence.

If it does not re-download, then **the KEPUB repair task has no effect on any
device that already has the book** — i.e. no effect on precisely the population
it exists to help, since a book has to have been synced to be broken on a device.

## The experiment that settles it

Cheap, and safe if scoped to a disposable book:
1. Pick a book already synced to the device that carries NO annotations.
2. Record the on-device file's size/mtime/hash.
3. Rewrite it server-side and bump `last_modified` only (exactly what the repair
   does — do NOT clear KoboSyncedBooks).
4. Sync. Re-measure the on-device file.
Changed bytes => ChangedEntitlement re-delivers and the repair works as intended.
Unchanged => the repair is invisible to already-synced devices and needs
`unsync=True` (or another delivery mechanism) to do anything at all.

Run the same experiment a second time WITH the synced row cleared, to find out
what `do_kobo_resend` is actually relying on.

## Do not "fix" this by flipping unsync=True until that is measured

Forcing re-delivery of every repaired book is not obviously safe: re-delivery
changes spine filenames for split/normalized packages, and the device's existing
Bookmark rows are matched by ContentID. A forced redownload could strand
highlights that currently still render. Measure first.
title: KEPUB repair may never reach a device that already has the book, and two places document a mechanism the code does not implement
